persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Brian, 64. Every Saturday you play pickleball with four friends: Tom, Linda, Carol and Dave. Every week you ask in a group text who is coming, the answers get lost between other messages, and you never know how many will come. Today you try Who's Coming instead.

challenge.intro: Now you are Brian. The app must start empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press: use what you learned. You do NOT need to send any real message and you do NOT need anyone's real number. If your messages app opens, go back to Who's Coming without pressing Send. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open Who’s Coming. This app is not in the house erase list, so there is no 🧹 Start fresh link at the bottom. Instead: 1) If the welcome tour shows by itself, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, tap the ? button at the bottom right → '🎬 Take the tour again' → 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. This removes the example group and question. 2) On the ❓ Asks tab, tap 🗑 on every question that is left → OK. 3) On the 👥 People tab, tap 'Remove group' on every group that is left → OK. (The 'Me' box cannot be emptied; that is fine, the first task changes it.) The Asks tab now says 'Nothing asked yet'.

tasks.text: Answers must come back to you. Put in your name, Brian, and your mobile number, 847-555-0123.
tasks.hint: Look on the People tab, in the box called 'Me — so replies come back to you'. Then tap Save.

tasks.text: Make a group called Pickleball group with your four friends in it: Tom, Linda, Carol and Dave. Numbers are not needed.
tasks.hint: On the People tab, make the group first. Then add each friend inside that group's card.

tasks.text: Ask the Pickleball group: Practice on Saturday at 3pm, are you coming? They should be able to answer Yes, No or Maybe.
tasks.hint: On the Asks tab, tap '＋ Ask the group something'. Check 'Who are you asking?' says Pickleball group.

tasks.text: Your friends told you face to face: Tom is coming, Linda is not coming, and Carol is not sure. Dave has not answered. Record this in the app.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dj_whoscoming_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.asks))return false;var gs=d.groups||[];return d.asks.some(function(a){if(a.kind!=='yn')return false;var g=gs.filter(function(x){return x.id===a.groupId})[0];if(!g||!/pickleball/i.test(String(g.name||'')))return false;var A=a.answers||{};function ans(nm){var p=(g.people||[]).filter(function(x){return String(x.name||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(nm)>=0})[0];return p&&A[p.id]?String(A[p.id].a):''}return ans('tom')==='Yes'&&ans('linda')==='No'&&ans('carol')==='Maybe'&&ans('dave')===''})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Find the practice question's card on the Asks tab. Each friend has their own row of answer buttons.

tasks.text: Also ask the Pickleball group which day is better for the tournament: Saturday or Sunday. They must choose one of those two days.
tasks.hint: Make a new question, and under 'How can they answer?' choose 'Pick one'. Type each day on its own line.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: ask one group one question, like who is coming
see everyone's answer on one screen: yes, no, maybe, or not yet
it uses your own text messages, and you record or nudge the answers

lines: Welcome. In about four minutes, you will know what Who's Coming is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. You want to ask a group one simple question, like Sunday lunch at one, who's coming? So you send it to the group text.
The answers come back mixed in with jokes and photos. Some people answer twice, some forget, and you end up counting on your fingers.
Who's Coming solves that. You ask one question to one group, and the app keeps every person's answer on one screen: yes, no, maybe, and who hasn't answered yet.
Who is it for? A family planning a lunch. A church choir. A team choosing a practice night. Anyone who organizes people.
It uses your phone's own text messages. Nothing is sent unless you press Send yourself, and nobody has to sign up to answer.
Here is the layout. At the bottom are two tabs. Asks is where your questions are. People is where your groups are.
At the top is the helper card. The first time, it asks your name and mobile number, because answers come back to that number.
Start on the People tab. Each group is a card. The first time, there is one example group to show you how it looks.
Under New group, type a group name, like Sunday lunch crew, and tap Add group.
Inside the new group, type a name and tap Add, one person at a time. A mobile number is optional, but it lets the app text them.
Or tap Paste a list, type one person on each line, and tap Add them all. From contacts brings people in from your phone.
Rename changes a group's name. The small x takes one person out. Remove group asks first, and its questions stay on the Asks tab.
Further down, under Me, you can save your name and number too.
Now go to the Asks tab and tap the big button, Ask the group something.
First, choose who you are asking.
Then type the question. Keep it short, like: Sunday lunch at one, who's coming?
Then choose how they answer: Yes, No, Maybe. Or Pick one, with your choices typed one per line. Or In their own words.
Answer by is optional. Put a date if you need the answers by then.
Tap Save and send. If your group has mobile numbers, your messages app opens one group text with a link to tap. You press Send. With no numbers, the app copies the message for you to paste anywhere.
When someone taps the link, they see your question with big answer buttons. Tapping one opens a text back to you, with their answer already typed in.
Now the important part. Your question becomes a card on the Asks tab, with answer buttons by each person. When someone tells you their answer, by text, phone or face to face, tap it on the card.
The card counts the answers at the top: how many yes, how many no, how many maybe. People who haven't answered show not yet. If you tap the wrong one, the x clears it.
Nudge the quiet ones reminds only the people who haven't answered. Copy the tally copies every name and answer. Close puts the question away.
How to start: put in your name and number, make one real group with three people, and ask them one question.
Everything stays on this phone. There is no account and there are no ads. Who's Coming is free.
The question mark button in the corner has the tour and help, any time.
And every Daraja app helps a student in Kenya stay in school. Happy asking.

daily.task: Add one guest in Who’s Coming, or change one guest’s answer.
